article.title: Lattice plainification and band engineering lead to high thermoelectric cooling and power generation in n-type Bi2Te3 with mass production

acquisition.note: Europe PMC mirrors the PMC11737397 open-access record; used because the PMC binary endpoint served a proof-of-work page on the acquisition date.

evidence_locations.n_material: Article Fig. 2(a,c) and Fig. 5(a): n-type BTS+0.2%Cu
evidence_locations.p_material: Supplementary Fig. S9, PDF page 17 / printed S17: p-type commercial BST
evidence_locations.transport_measurement_uncertainty: Supplementary PDF page 3 / printed S3: S and sigma within 5%; page 4 / printed S4: kappa within about 8%
evidence_locations.geometry_and_assembly: Supplementary PDF pages 4-5 / printed S4-S5: 1.95 x 1.95 x 4.8 mm3 legs, 7 pairs, Ni electroplating, Sn-Ag-Cu solder, copper aluminium nitride ceramics, 10 x 10 x 6 mm3 device
evidence_locations.cooling_test: Supplementary PDF page 5 / printed S5: Z-Meters with reference temperatures 303 K and 343 K
evidence_locations.device_resistance: Article Fig. 6(d) and Supplementary Fig. S11: 0.131 ohm at about 303 K and 0.164 ohm at about 343 K for BTS+0.2%Cu/BST
evidence_locations.n_contact_resistivity: Article Fig. 6(c): approximately 3.5 micro-ohm cm2 across the displayed Cu-to-BTS+0.2%Cu contact stack

explicit_absences: No author-supplied numerical transport table is attached.
No p/n measurement covariance or repeat-level data are reported.
No complete p-leg contact-resistance inventory is reported.
No numerical thermal-contact resistance or parasitic thermal conductance is reported.
The cooling maximum reaches below the 300 K lower limit of the published transport curves; no sub-300-K extrapolation is allowed here.
The numerical fields visible in the Z-Meter screenshots are not assigned physical labels unless the article or caption names them.
